chunks: From him, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abdullah ibn Ayn who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! A Christian dies and he has a Muslim son, would he inherit him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not increase him with Islam except for honour, so we inherit them, but they do not inherit us.'

key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيُّ: Christian (specifically referring to the People of the Book in this context)

ai.seo_question: Does a Muslim son inherit from his Christian father according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the asymmetrical inheritance rule between Muslims and People of the Book, specifically noting that a Muslim son inherits from his Christian father. The Imam grounds this ruling in the divine principle that Islam confers honor ('izz), thereby elevating the Muslim's status such that they inherit from non-Muslims, but not vice versa. This distinction underscores the theological and social hierarchy established in Shia jurisprudence regarding religious affiliation.

en.hubeali: From him, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Abdullah Bin Ayn who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The Christian died and for him was a Muslim son, would he inherit him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not Increase with Al-Islam except for honour, so we inherit them, but they do not inherit us’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Musa ibn Bakr from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘A’yan who has narrated the following:

“I once said to abu Ja’far, Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, if a Christian man dies and has a Muslim son, can he inherit from him?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, because Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, through al-Islam has increased his honor, so we inherit from them but they cannot inherit from us.’”
